text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PD: INC-9012 fired for service=hosted-inference (elevated 429 throttles). Paging primary oncall: matt. Escalation policy: primary -> secondary (jen) -> manager (sre-lead). Duplicate suppress window: 90s.

matt: Acked on desktop. I see a sudden rise in 429s starting 04:12 UTC across edge LB -> gateway. Pulling logs.

jen: I didn't get the first page (my phone was in DND). incidentbot: 60s: no follow-up from primary in escalation window, paging secondary: jen.

matt: actually I acked but then switched to DND accidentally (driving). Sorry, brief delay — continue without me?

incidentbot: 30s: escalation to manager due to secondary delayed ack window. Paging sre-lead.

leo: Joining. Also noticed a flurry of PD pages for the same alert from two different rules (rate-limit and upstream-backpressure) — looks like the alert dedupe didn't catch it. Filed a quick note.

sre-lead: Joining bridge: https://call.redwood.ai/bridge/INC-9012. Who has context?

jen: I'm on mobile and taking primary. Quick triage: 429s are coming from our edge LB returning "X-RateLimit-Status: throttled" for inference requests. Most 429s spike during a single autoscale event: several inference pods entered Terminating state and HPA didn't bring new pods quickly.

ops-tilly: We just shipped an HPA target change at 04:05 (to reduce burst CPU target from 70% to 55%). Canary looked fine but the change reduced buffer headroom. Reverting now.

jen: Mitigation plan: (1) revert HPA change to previous target, (2) temporarily increase replica count min=6 -> 10, (3) enable emergency routing to dedicated-us-west to shed some traffic. Implementing steps 1+2.

```
# revert HPA and scale
kubectl patch hpa inference-deployment -n inference -p '{"spec":{"targetCPUUtilizationPercentage":70}}'
kubectl scale deployment inference-deployment -n inference --replicas=10
```

jen: Executed. Pods are spinning up. Watching readiness.

incidentbot: 3m: manager acknowledged. Note: PagerDuty detected duplicate pages suppressed: 2 duplicates suppressed in 90s window.

matt: I'm back on the bridge. Sorry for the DND confusion. Good mitigation plan. Two notes: (1) add preflight check for HPA changes, (2) fix alert dedupe to group by deployment+alert_type.

leo: Readiness probes are showing longer startup times due to a recent model warmup change. We should tweak readiness threshold to avoid marking pods ready too late or earlier depending on restart behavior. Increasing parallel warmup concurrency to speed start.

jen: After scaling, 429s drop to baseline in ~4 minutes. Metrics: 429 rate map https://metrics/hosted-inference/alerts/INC-9012. Error budget impact minimal but customer-facing alpha cohort did see increased failed calls.

customer-success: Sent interim customer note to alpha beta group: "We experienced transient throttling affecting some requests. We increased capacity and reverted a configuration change; service has stabilized. We'll follow up with details and an RCA."

incidentbot: PD INC-9012 status: acknowledged by jen -> resolved by jen at 04:25 UTC. Resolution note: reverted HPA target, scaled replicas, enabled emergency routing; follow-up RCA assigned to ops-tilly + leo.

sre-lead: Good. Action items: (1) ops-tilly - add HPA-change preflight and rollback automation, (2) leo - tune model warmup/readiness and document startup cost, (3) matt - own alert dedupe/PD rule grouping. I'll create a tracking ticket and schedule a 1hr RCA tomorrow.

matt: Will draft PD notes and attach the sequence of kubectl commands and scaling events. Also queue a postmortem doc.

jen: Leaving bridge but staying available if anything regresses. Thanks for the quick patching, team. :white_check_mark:

incidentbot: Thread closed; bridge remains open for follow-up until RCA.
